newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S DE KLERK SAYS STRIKE BAD FOR INVESTMENT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S DE KLERK SAYS STRIKE BAD FOR INVESTMENT.

text.p: Opposition leader F.W. de Klerk said on Monday the Congress of South African Trade Union's one-day strike over planned labour laws was detrimental to the country's bid for foreign investment.

Urging the African National Congress not to yield to pressure from the labour movement, de Klerk said the government's commitment to its Growth, Employment and Redistribution (GEAR) strategy was being tested.

"Cosatu is insisting on privileges which will exacerbate South Africa's lack of competitivity and which will inhibit new investment," de Klerk, the leader of the former ruling National Party, told the Cape Town Press Club.
"The coming weeks and months will be the acid test of the ANC government's commitment to GEAR and economic growth. The time has arrived to cut the power of the unions down to size...
"If the ANC fails us in this regard, all South Africans will pay dearly and our hopes of becoming a winning nation will evaporate," de Klerk said.
The 24-hour strike was called in protest against the planned Basic Conditions of Employment Bill, which was approved by the cabinet in April.

The bill sets a 45 hour working week and four months maternity leave. Cosatu, the biggest union federation with 1.9 million members, wants a 40 hour week, six months maternity leave and the minimum age for formal employment to be set at 18.
